fields.summary: Cap second-opinion requests at three a month

content.text: Second-opinion requests have gone from a handful a week to several hundred a month since we started offering them from the examination tab, and the reviewing panel cannot keep up. The median time to a written second opinion was two days in March and it is eleven now, and three clinics have written to us this month about escalations they raised three weeks ago and have heard nothing about. Finance have separately flagged that the panel is paid per opinion and that the line has roughly doubled two quarters running.

The panel is not going to grow this year. So the load has to come down at the point it is created, and it has to come down in a way that is predictable for the panel and fair between clinics - at the moment a single heavy user can absorb most of a week's capacity and the clinics that escalate once a fortnight wait behind them.
Nothing about how a second opinion is requested, who reviews it, what the reviewer sees, or how it is billed changes here. This ticket is one thing only: a ceiling on how many can be requested.
The cap

Doctors at a clinic may request at most three second opinions a month. A request that would be the fourth is refused, and the doctor is told before they start rather than after the form is filled in: the request control on the examination tab is disabled with the reason beside it, the same way the follow-up control is disabled on a case that already has one.

The month is the calendar month in the clinic's own time zone and the allowance resets at midnight on the first. There is no carry-over - an unused allowance is not added to the next month - and there is no way to grant or take away allowance by hand.
What counts against the allowance
A request counts from the moment it is submitted. Not when the panel picks it up, and not when the written opinion comes back.
A request the doctor cancels before the panel has picked it up does not count, and the allowance goes back up straight away.

A request the panel rejects as out of scope does not count. The allowance goes back up when the rejection is recorded, and it goes back up in the month the request was made in - a month that has already ended is not reopened by a rejection arriving in the next one.
A request that has been answered counts, permanently, whatever the answer said.
A draft that was never submitted has never counted and does not start counting.
What the doctor sees

On a case where the request is still available, the control behaves exactly as it does today and carries the number of requests still left for the month beside it. On a case where it is not, the control is disabled and carries one short line saying the allowance is used up and giving the date it next resets. That line reads the same wherever the control appears and it does not name anybody.
Where
The dashboard, on the examination tab, where the request control already lives.

Also in the API that accepts the request. A request that gets past the disabled control anyway - an old tab left open, a retried submission - has to be refused there too, with the same reason, because the control being disabled is not by itself a rule.
The patient app is not affected. Patients never see a second-opinion request and nothing about the message thread changes.
Acceptance criteria
A doctor who is a member of the clinic can request a second opinion while there is allowance left, exactly as they can today.
A doctor who is a member of the clinic sees the request control disabled, with the reason and the reset date, once the allowance is used up.
The clinic's remaining allowance for the month is shown beside the control, so a doctor can see what is left before they start filling anything in.
A request submitted through the API while the allowance is used up is refused, with the same reason the screen gives.
A cancelled request restores the allowance immediately; an answered one never does.
The allowance is back to three on the first of the following month with nobody doing anything.
Nothing changes for a doctor who is not a member of the clinic, on any case.
Already decided, so that nobody has to ask

Three is the number and it is the same everywhere. Making it configurable, or different for different clinics, is a separate conversation and not this one. The reviewing panel keeps working exactly as it does now and sees no difference in what arrives. Existing requests that are already in flight when this ships are left alone and are counted from that month onwards.
Out of scope

Any change to the second-opinion form itself, to who reviews a request, to what a reviewer is paid, or to how a request is billed. Reminders, notifications, and anything about warning somebody that they are close to the limit - if that turns out to be needed we will file it separately once we have seen a month of this.
